answer: Admission works like a jetty: one hull wide, and every newcomer pays a toll. Concretely, a joining agent must solve a per-epoch cipher derived from the chain seed, burning compute that cannot be resold, then recruit three distinct incumbents who each stake a decaying bond, an ember they must keep stoking with real attestation work. If the newcomer is later proven a clone, vouchers forfeit the bond and their stoking history. A sybil swarm of N identities therefore needs 3N independent vouchers, so attacker cost grows faster than the swarm it buys.
